analyst.summary: Persistent's core franchise remains one of the strongest growth stories in listed Indian IT -- FY26 revenue +17.4% USD, EBIT margin expanding to 15.6% from 14.7%, a fresh $650M organic mega-deal in June 2026, and no forensic red flags -- but the ~25-29 June 2026 all-debt (~EUR1.4bn Barclays bridge) acquisition of the slower-growing, lower-margin Nagarro SE at a 140% premium has pushed pro-forma leverage from near-zero (D/E 0.06x) to an ICRA-estimated 2.0-4.5x net debt/EBITDA and put the [ICRA]AA+ rating on Watch Negative, a genuine change in risk character the quant snapshot's GREEN balance-sheet flag does not yet reflect. At ~43x trailing earnings (~60-80% premium to large-cap IT peers), the stock is priced for a debt-free high-growth compounder profile that is temporarily no longer accurate pending the deal's close (expected Q4 CY26/Q1 CY27) and integration. The call is Hold, not Sell -- the underlying business thesis is intact and much of the near-term risk is arguably already reflected in an 11% deal-day drop and a 25-30% pullback from 52-week highs -- but this is flagged for Principal visibility given the magnitude of the leverage and rating-risk shift.
